note: e3/e4 (shaded vs open habitat -> fewer emerged/surviving seedlings) concern seedlings of wd:Q5122070, whose identity as a willow-family (Salicaceae) species is not stated in the text; other seedling edges are black spruce/balsam fir. Left out.

e1/e2 compare fish presence (invasive non-native fish vs vacant sites) on herpetofauna wetland richness, not genetic origin of fish, and herpetofauna are not stated to be vulnerable species; e3/e4 are genic diversity/allelic richness, not species richness.

Near misses from study 10.1111/j.1526-100X.1995.tb00096.x: e7/e26/e27 show nitrogen decreasing density of native (not specifically grass) seedlings; density is not survival. If accepted as proxies they would vote -1.
Soil mixing edges (MSM, forest floor mixing) are on black spruce (conifer) only; hardwood seedling size edges (apsoil study) concern soil inoculation, not soil mixing.
Mulch edges report root-to-shoot ratio, survivorship, establishment or biomass, not seedling height:diameter ratio; none are straw mulch.
No edge measures large tree abundance; e41 (direct placement vs stockpiling of cover soil -> tree cover) is the closest but neither side matches.
CRF edges (study 10.1016/j.foreco.2015.10.024) report growth and nutrient outcomes, not emergence; e12 is generic fertilization -> deciduous seedling establishment.
e3 (slash cover -> lower vegetation cover) concerns vegetation cover, not bare ground cover.

e30/e33/e36 (study 10.1111/j.1526-100X.2007.00209.x: disturbance treatments reduced cover of dominant grasses Poa and Dactylis) excluded because the text does not state these grasses are non-native; if counted as non-native they would vote -1 and direction would become mixed (certainty low).
e1/e2 run organic matter -> macroinvertebrate abundance (reversed) and concern stream particulate organic matter, not soil.
